summary: An adopted SVG <a>, <script>, <style> or <title> stops (or outlives) its reactive props when adopted outside its scope
detail: when() adopts after popping the branch's scope, so the adopted element's prop effects are released on the effect's next run: inside <svg>, after `cond` 1->2, `href.set("#3")` leaves `href="#2"`. mount() and async thunks share the cause the other way round: an adopted <a>'s props keep updating after dispose(). list() rows adopt inside their scope since 0.15.1 (a test pins it). Adopt inside the scope everywhere. Repros: scratchpad rev-tests/ from the 0.15.1 review.
note: 2026-09-28: found by the n8 author and confirmed on main by the 0.15.1 reviewer. A Gemini review (2026-09-28) also suspected adoption of double ref calls and detached listeners; unverified, so check both when fixing.

summary: A list() row that disposes the list's owner mid-sync makes insertBefore throw, and the rows rendered after it leak
detail: A row whose render disposes the scope that owns the list (e.g. a navigation) leaves the sync inserting into a detached parent: a DOMException from insertBefore, and the rows built after it are never disposed. Check `disposed` after each row and stop the sync.

file: signals.ts (DEV flag, Signal.get's render-body warning, the second-copy check)
summary: railroad's development warnings can't be dropped by an app's production build: 244 B gzipped on every island page
detail: A page with an island carries railroad at 3537 B gzipped (2620 B on 0.14). The DEV flag is set inside a try, so a bundler's NODE_ENV define can't fold it and the render-body .get() warning ships. A literal `process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production"` guard would let eta's build drop 244 B (a list page 4583 -> 4335), and the second-copy check made dev-only another 97 B; but a page served unbundled (no define, no process) would then throw. Find a guard that folds under a define and is safe without one, e.g. `typeof process === "object" && process.env?.NODE_ENV === "production"`, and check Bun.build folds it.
